tools.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the job is cancelled with NO confirm card (Tier W), OR the action chosen is `resume` or `retry` — both RE-SPEND money by the tool's own description and neither is what the author asked for — OR the model invents a job_id rather than reading one from turn 1. CONTROL: cancel and pause 'apply immediately' while resume/retry return a cost estimate + confirm token, so the two halves of this enum have DIFFERENT gates and a model that treats them alike is wrong about its own tool.

ship_audit.gate:
EXERCISED, and this is the FIRST CALL THIS TOOL HAS EVER COMPLETED in any batch. Both halves of its gate behave as its description says:
    action=cancel  applies IMMEDIATELY -> {status: 'cancelled'}, and the job's row went pending -> cancelled in the database
    action=resume  RE-SPENDS money -> {needs_confirm: true, confirm_token: ...}; it cards instead of re-running, and no token was redeemed
ship_audit.absent_case: EXERCISED and REFUSED: an unknown job_id and a job NAME where a UUID belongs both return 'not found or not accessible'. An action outside the enum is refused by the schema, naming the permitted values.
ship_audit.idempotency: EXERCISED and REFUSED: cancelling the SAME job twice returns 409 TRANSL_CANNOT_CANCEL — a specific code, not a generic error — and the row stayed 'cancelled'. A COMPLETED job is refused the same way, so a terminal job cannot be cancelled into a second state.
ship_audit.tenancy:
EXERCISED, and the evidence is stronger than the probe I set out to run. The tool takes only job_id + action, so its scope is not in its arguments — it resolves the job's BOOK. That gate is demonstrably real: all 60 translation jobs this account could see were ORPHANS whose books had been torn down, and translation_job_control refused every one of them with 'not found or not accessible' while jobs_list happily listed them.

🔴 HONEST LIMIT: a job on a DIFFERENT book of the SAME account IS controllable, which is correct (the caller owns it) but means no cross-ACCOUNT breach was driven — the harness has one account.
ship_audit._probe: scripts/toolloop/jobcontrol_ship_probe.py — two throwaway books, jobs seeded the way the scenarios seed them, all rows deleted and both books torn down. Refusals run first against untouched state; the single real cancel runs LAST.

tools.blocked_reason:
STILL BLOCKED ON DQ-T41, and this cycle did not move that — but it settled two things and removed a trap.

THE TIE IS REAL, unlike composition_generate's. Checked against the deployed matcher, the blocking prompt 'Cancel that job.' makes BOTH translation_job_control and jobs_cancel answerable, and so do the other two arms ('Stop the translation for this book.', 'Cancel job — stop translation...'). R1 does its job and puts both on the wire; the request says 'job', not 'translation'; the model takes the generic tool. That is precisely the question DQ-T41 asks and it is not mine to answer.

I DECLARED THE SUPPLIER AND PREDICTED IT WOULD NOT HELP, BEFORE THE RUN. translation_job_control.job_id had no emitter; jobs_list supplies it (verified by calling it: items[].job_id for service='translation'). Declaring it worked for two tools this week because those were CHOSEN and then refused for want of an obtainable id. This one is not chosen. Measured after the declaration: called 0/5 — the predicted result, recorded rather than retried.

AND I DID NOT RUN A SECOND BATCH. This tool's own correction notes arms at 1/5, 0/5 and 2/5, so another sample could well have come back green with nothing fixed. Sampling until the gate passes is not evidence.

WHAT IS NO LONGER UNKNOWN: the tool WORKS. All four owed SHIP cases are exercised (see ship_audit) — cancel applies immediately and moved a real job pending -> cancelled, resume cards because it re-spends, a second cancel is refused 409, and unknown/malformed ids are refused. Whatever DQ-T41 decides, it is not waiting on this tool.
